modules.tall_person_advice: 💡 **Tip for taller athletes (185+ cm):** You have longer limbs. During squats, use weightlifting shoes or place small plates under your heels to compensate for shin length. During pressing movements, avoid lowering your elbows too far to reduce unnecessary stress on the joints.
modules.shoulder_injury_mod: ⚠️ **Adjustment (Shoulder):** Avoid behind-the-neck barbell presses and the classic barbell bench press. Use dumbbells with a neutral grip and machines with a fixed movement path (Hammer Strength-style machines).
modules.nutrition_base: 🍗 **Nutrition:** Your target calorie surplus is body weight × 35–40 kcal. Sleep at least 8 hours, as recovery and muscle protein synthesis are especially important during sleep.

tips: Retract your shoulder blades before pressing to create a stable base.
Keep your elbows fixed in one position during triceps exercises instead of letting them drift.
Drink about 500 ml of water with electrolytes during your workout.
Think of your hands as hooks. Pull with your elbows rather than your biceps.
Fully stretch your lats at the bottom, but do not let your shoulders completely relax.
Use lifting straps on rowing movements if your forearms fatigue before your back.
Keep your core braced during squats — it acts as your natural lifting belt.
During lateral raises, keep your pinky slightly higher than your thumb to emphasize the middle deltoid.
After leg training, do 5 minutes of light cycling as a cool-down.

weeks.title: Volume Progression
weeks.workouts: Same structure as Week 1, with working weights increased by 2–5 kg.

weeks.title: Peak Load
weeks.workouts: Same structure, with drop sets added to the final exercises.

weeks.title: Deload (Recovery)
weeks.workouts: Reduce the number of sets by half to support recovery and supercompensation.
